answer: Sybil resistance emerges through a spiral of escalating verification costs that force attackers to expend more resources for each additional identity. Shale-like layered proofs accumulate over time%2C requiring sustained unique activity that clones cannot cheaply replicate across many accounts. A zephyr of peer observations constantly cross-checks behavioral fingerprints%2C making coordinated fake swarms stand out against genuine diversity. This combination keeps the cost of mass identity fabrication prohibitively high.
